1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος κλητὸς ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ καὶ Σωσθένης ὁ ἀδελφὸς
1:1.targetText: Paul, a called apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,

groups.note: The actual Christ/Jesus genitive name phrase is ordered Christ Jesus in the Greek and Jesus Christ in LSV; each name keeps its actual identity despite the order difference.

1:2.sourceText: τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ, ἡγιασμένοις ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις, σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐπικαλουμένοις τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, αὐτῶν καὶ ἡμῶν·
1:2.targetText: to the Assembly of God that is in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called holy ones, with all those calling on the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place—both theirs and ours:

groups.note: The actual perfect passive sanctified participle is dative plural with the addressed Assembly/people. English to those sanctified realizes its substantive personal construction without an independently printed those pronoun.
The actual plural holy adjective is substantival, rendered holy ones; no separate Greek ones noun is printed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly coordinates the two personal possessors with both; pinned N1904 prints theirs and ours without a separate both particle.

1:3.sourceText: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:3.targetText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!

1:4.sourceText: Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ δοθείσῃ ὑμῖν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,
1:4.targetText: I give thanks to my God always concerning you for the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly makes God my God. Pinned N1904 has the dative God phrase without an independently written first-person possessive here.

1:5.sourceText: ὅτι ἐν παντὶ ἐπλουτίσθητε ἐν αὐτῷ, ἐν παντὶ λόγῳ καὶ πάσῃ γνώσει,
1:5.targetText: that in everything you were enriched in Him, in all discourse and all knowledge,

1:6.sourceText: καθὼς τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐβεβαιώθη ἐν ὑμῖν,
1:6.targetText: according as the testimony of the Christ was confirmed in you,

1:7.sourceText: ὥστε ὑμᾶς μὴ ὑστερεῖσθαι ἐν μηδενὶ χαρίσματι, ἀπεκδεχομένους τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ·
1:7.targetText: so that you are not behind in any gift, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,

groups.note: Actual ὑστερεῖσθαι is the infinitive be-lacking/fall-short under so-that. English makes the same predicate finite as are ... behind; no independent Greek be verb is printed.

Actual μηδενί is the negative no/none determiner. English realizes the coordinated negative construction as not ... any: the explicit μή supplies not and μηδενί retains the any scope under that negation.

1:8.sourceText: ὃς καὶ βεβαιώσει ὑμᾶς ἕως τέλους ἀνεγκλήτους ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:8.targetText: who also will confirm you to the end—unblamable in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ;

1:9.sourceText: πιστὸς ὁ Θεὸς, δι’ οὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν.
1:9.targetText: faithful [is] God, through whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with God or our Lord in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula linking faithful and God. Pinned N1904 has the faithful adjective and God noun without a written be verb here.

1:10.sourceText: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ λέγητε πάντες, καὶ μὴ ᾖ ἐν ὑμῖν σχίσματα, ἦτε δὲ κατηρτισμένοι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ νοῒ καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ.
1:10.targetText: And I call on you, brothers, through the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that the same thing you may all say, and there may not be divisions among you, and you may be perfected in the same mind, and in the same judgment,

1:11.sourceText: ἐδηλώθη γάρ μοι περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί μου, ὑπὸ τῶν Χλόης, ὅτι ἔριδες ἐν ὑμῖν εἰσιν.
1:11.targetText: for it was signified to me concerning you, my brothers, by those of Chloe, that contentions are among you;

1:12.sourceText: λέγω δὲ τοῦτο, ὅτι ἕκαστος ὑμῶν λέγει Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, Ἐγὼ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ, Ἐγὼ δὲ Κηφᾶ, Ἐγὼ δὲ Χριστοῦ.
1:12.targetText: and I say this, that each one of you says, “I, indeed, am of Paul,” and “I of Apollos,” and “I of Cephas,” and “I of Christ.”

1:13.sourceText: μεμέρισται ὁ Χριστός; μὴ Παῦλος ἐσταυρώθη ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ἢ εἰς τὸ ὄνομα Παύλου ἐβαπτίσθητε;
1:13.targetText: Has the Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you immersed into the name of Paul?

unmappedSource.reason: Actual μή introduces the crucifixion question expecting a negative answer. English asks Was Paul crucified without separately rendering that negative question particle.

1:14.sourceText: εὐχαριστῶ ὅτι οὐδένα ὑμῶν ἐβάπτισα εἰ μὴ Κρίσπον καὶ Γάϊον·
1:14.targetText: I give thanks to God that I immersed no one of you, except Crispus and Gaius—

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names the recipient of thanksgiving. Pinned N1904 has I give thanks followed by that, without an independently written God recipient phrase in this verse.

1:15.sourceText: ἵνα μή τις εἴπῃ ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα ἐβαπτίσθητε.
1:15.targetText: that no one may say that to my own name I immersed;

groups.note: Actual ἐβαπτίσθητε is aorist passive second-person plural, you were immersed. English immersed retains the same immersion predicate but recasts it as first-person active; that separate I remains unpaired rather than changing the original person/voice analysis.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with my own name.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has a first-person active immersion statement. Pinned N1904 prints the passive second-person plural ἐβαπτίσθητε, you were immersed; the English first-person agent is not supplied by that source inflection.

1:16.sourceText: ἐβάπτισα δὲ καὶ τὸν Στεφανᾶ οἶκον· λοιπὸν οὐκ οἶδα εἴ τινα ἄλλον ἐβάπτισα.
1:16.targetText: and I also immersed Stephanas’ household—further, I have not known if I immersed any other.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with the possessed Stephanas household.

1:17.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἀπέστειλέν με Χριστὸς βαπτίζειν ἀλλὰ εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ λόγου, ἵνα μὴ κενωθῇ ὁ σταυρὸς τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:17.targetText: For Christ did not send me to immerse, but to proclaim good news, not in wisdom of discourse, that the Cross of the Christ may not be made of no effect;

1:18.sourceText: Ὁ λόγος γὰρ ὁ τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῖς μὲν ἀπολλυμένοις μωρία ἐστίν, τοῖς δὲ σῳζομένοις ἡμῖν δύναμις Θεοῦ ἐστιν.
1:18.targetText: for the word of the Cross to those indeed perishing is foolishness, and to us—those being saved—it is the power of God,

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated Greek attributive article introduces the Cross qualifier of word; English does not separately render that second article.

1:19.sourceText: γέγραπται γάρ Ἀπολῶ τὴν σοφίαν τῶν σοφῶν, καὶ τὴν σύνεσιν τῶν συνετῶν ἀθετήσω.
1:19.targetText: for it has been written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the intelligence of the intelligent I will bring to nothing”;

1:20.sourceText: ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ γραμματεύς; ποῦ συνζητητὴς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου; οὐχὶ ἐμώρανεν ὁ Θεὸς τὴν σοφίαν τοῦ κόσμου;
1:20.targetText: where [is] the wise? Where the scribe? Where a disputer of this age? Did God not make foolish the wisdom of this world?

groups.note: The actual wise adjective is substantival, rendered the wise for the person characterized by wisdom; no separate Greek wise-person noun is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God in the question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the initial copula in the series of where questions; the Greek has no independent be verb in this verse.
LSV explicitly qualifies the final world noun with this. Pinned N1904 has the world genitive phrase without a demonstrative at this final position.

1:21.sourceText: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἔγνω ὁ κόσμος διὰ τῆς σοφίας τὸν Θεόν, εὐδόκησεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ τῆς μωρίας τοῦ κηρύγματος σῶσαι τοὺς πιστεύοντας.
1:21.targetText: For seeing in the wisdom of God the world through the wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the preaching to save those believing.

groups.note: Actual ἐπειδή is the causal conjunction, rendered seeing in the English seeing-that sense. No Greek visual seeing verb is printed at this position.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with the second and third God mentions.

1:22.sourceText: ἐπειδὴ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι σημεῖα αἰτοῦσιν καὶ Ἕλληνες σοφίαν ζητοῦσιν,
1:22.targetText: Since also Jews ask a sign, and Greeks seek wisdom,

groups.note: Actual σημεῖα is plural signs, while LSV uses singular a sign for the requested sign category. The shared sign noun retains its original plural form analysis.

1:23.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ κηρύσσομεν Χριστὸν ἐσταυρωμένον, Ἰουδαίοις μὲν σκάνδαλον, ἔθνεσιν δὲ μωρίαν,
1:23.targetText: also we preach Christ crucified, to Jews, indeed, a stumbling-block, and to Greeks foolishness,

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 has ἔθνεσιν, nations/Gentiles, as the second addressed group. LSV instead names Greeks, a different written group name rather than the actual Greek Ἕλληνες lemma at this position.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV names Greeks where pinned N1904 names nations/Gentiles. The two labels are not falsely assigned the same printed Greek lexical head.

1:24.sourceText: αὐτοῖς δὲ τοῖς κλητοῖς, Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν, Χριστὸν Θεοῦ δύναμιν καὶ Θεοῦ σοφίαν.
1:24.targetText: and to those called—both Jews and Greeks—Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God,

groups.note: The actual dative emphatic αὐτοῖς with article-and-called adjective forms the substantive to-those-called group. English retains that addressed group without an independently repeated emphatic same/them word.

1:25.sourceText: ὅτι τὸ μωρὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ σοφώτερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐστίν, καὶ τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἰσχυρότερον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
1:25.targetText: because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men;

groups.note: The actual article plus foolish adjective is substantival, rendered the foolishness; the original remains that adjective construction rather than a separately printed μωρία foolishness noun.

One actual singular be predicate is written in the coordinated comparison. English repeats is with each same-form comparison; both repeats retain that one actual source identity without inventing a second be verb.
The actual article plus weak adjective is substantival, rendered the weakness; no separate ἀσθένεια weakness noun is printed.

1:26.sourceText: Βλέπετε γὰρ τὴν κλῆσιν ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι οὐ πολλοὶ σοφοὶ κατὰ σάρκα, οὐ πολλοὶ δυνατοί, οὐ πολλοὶ εὐγενεῖς·
1:26.targetText: for see your calling, brothers, that not many [are] wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your calling.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula for the characterization of the called people. Pinned N1904 has the adjective series without a separately written be verb.

1:27.sourceText: ἀλλὰ τὰ μωρὰ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τοὺς σοφούς, καὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ τοῦ κόσμου ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός ἵνα καταισχύνῃ τὰ ἰσχυρά,
1:27.targetText: but God chose the foolish things of the world that He may put the wise to shame; and God chose the weak things of the world that He may put the strong to shame;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with the two God subjects.

1:28.sourceText: καὶ τὰ ἀγενῆ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὰ ἐξουθενημένα ἐξελέξατο ὁ Θεός, τὰ μὴ ὄντα, ἵνα τὰ ὄντα καταργήσῃ,
1:28.targetText: and God chose the base things of the world, and the things despised, and the things that are not, that He may make useless the things that are—

groups.note: The actual being participle supplies the things-that-are substantive predicate, negated separately by μή; the English nominal/relative support does not introduce independent Greek things or that words.
The actual being participle supplies the English things-that-are expression; it is kept distinct from the earlier negated being participle.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an explicit conjunction before the things that are not. Pinned N1904 places that phrase in apposition after the preceding selected things, without a separate καί at this position.

1:29.sourceText: ὅπως μὴ καυχήσηται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
1:29.targetText: that no flesh may glory before Him;

groups.note: The actual μή plus πᾶσα universal-negative construction is rendered no with flesh; no standalone οὐδείς none pronoun is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 explicitly names God in the before-God phrase. LSV uses the personal pronoun Him; that pronominal wording is left distinct from the written Θεός noun. Pinned CrossWire TR at1Cor.1.29 instead prints αὐτοῦ, corroborating the actual named/pronominal reading difference rather than a translation-publisher expansion.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has the personal pronoun Him where pinned N1904 explicitly names God. No written Greek αὐτός pronoun is invented for this source position.

1:30.sourceText: ἐξ αὐτοῦ δὲ ὑμεῖς ἐστε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὃς ἐγενήθη σοφία ἡμῖν ἀπὸ Θεοῦ, δικαιοσύνη τε καὶ ἁγιασμὸς καὶ ἀπολύτρωσις,
1:30.targetText: but out of Him you are in Christ Jesus, who became to us from God wisdom, righteousness also, and sanctification, and redemption,

1:31.sourceText: ἵνα καθὼς γέγραπται Ὁ καυχώμενος ἐν Κυρίῳ καυχάσθω.
1:31.targetText: that, according as it has been written: “He who is glorying—let him glory in the LORD.”
